of both body and spirit. 
St. Basi l the Great  says, “By fasting, Elijah became a spectator of a great spectacle 
[wonder]. For after he purified his soul through a forty -day fast, he was deemed worthy of 
seeing the Lord in the cave on Horeb, insofar as it is possible for a human being to se e the 
Lord (see 1 Kings 19:8 –13). While fasting, he restored the child to the widow, fasting 
granting him power over death (see 1 Kings 17:17–24).”417 
1019. What is the link between fasting and the friends of the bridegroom? 
Why did Christ our Lord say, “Can the friends of the bridegroom mourn as long as the 
bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away 
from them, and then they will fast” (Matt. 9:15) ? The purpose of fasting is to admit us to 
the Bridegroom’s presence where we can enjoy the wedding through repentance.  For if the 
Bridegroom Himself is present, why should they  fast? But w hen He ascends bodily and 
leaves them, then the Church fasts adorning herself for His second coming when she will be 
united with Him in the eternal wedding. As long as the Bridegroom is ascended, we do not 
see Him in the flesh,  and we must fast from every pleasure and luxury that we may  attain 
the superior heavenly nourishment , and exalted glories whose essence is union with the 
Bridegroom Himself. St. Basil the Great  believes that fasting lifts the soul up to heaven, 
“as if it were its  wings for the upwards journey” and it is “ adornment for seniors, a good 
companion on journeys.”418 
If one visits his brother after a long absence tha t lasted for decades, and the visit was 
unexpected so that his brother was eating when he came, would we not expect the brother 
to leave what he is eating, no matter how hungry he was, to embrace his brother? What a 
joyful surprise this would be!  Likewise, by fasting we leave our tables, not as way of 
asceticism, but more because of our preoccupation with the Heavenly One, that we may 
encounter Him, enter into sweet conversation with Him, express our longing for Him, and 
escape the distractions of our bodily needs.  
1020. Why does the Creator call us to practice the way of the angels? 
When humans enslaved their souls to their bellies, they were deprived of  the Garden of 
Eden. However, God’s desire is not to call the children of Adam to an earthly garden but to 
a heavenly paradise, where we will not need either food or drink. Thus, fasting is a sign of 
the believer’s joyful acceptance of this calling. 
St. Gregory of Nyssa  says, “As the resurrection holds forth to us a life equal with the 
angels, and with the angels there is no food, there is sufficient ground for believing that

1029. What is the purpose of fasting?  
First. Acquisition of virtues: St. Jerome says, “Fasting is not itself an absolute virtue, 
but the foundation of virtues.” 
Second. Motivation to give thanks : St. Evagrius believes that the person who fasts 
becomes aware of the grace of God at work within him : “Those who excessively feed their 
bodies to fulfil their desires (Rom. 13:14) … when they become no longer lustful, although 
they remain in the same body; and when they become active in their contemplation o f the 
One God , the true Being, as much as possible ; such people confess the Creator’s 
graciousness to them, for He granted them this body.” 
Third. Appreciation of food as a blessing : St. Basil believes that while fasting is an 
opportunity to abstain from food, then end of fasting is an opportunity for rejoicing  in food 
— not with excessive indulgence, but with a sense of the blessedness of food. “After all, 
just as thirst makes drinking pleasurable and hunger before a meal makes eating 
pleasurable, so too fasting enhances the enjoyment of food when it is partake n … Don’t 
you realize that … health is more appreciated after the experience of the contrary? So too is 
the table more charming after fasting.”447 
Fourth. Freedom from enslavement to one’s belly: Abba Theonas says, “We never 
read that anyone is condemned simply for taking food, but only when something was joined 
with it or followed afterwards, for which he deserved condemnation. ”448 And St. John 
Climacus says, “Master your stomach before it masters you.”449 
1030. Why does the Church conclude most of her fasts with a relevant feast? 
The purpose of fasting is to  enable us to  enjoy the heavenly feast , or to experience 
heavenly joy. During our fasts, our minds are immersed in rejoicing  in the Lord of Glory, 
Jesus, who was born to offer us His life as heavenly bread to sa tisfy our souls. We are 
occupied with His salvific work by which He granted us the resurrection of our souls , 
which were undone by death and corrupted by destructive sin.  
In his fasts, the true believer does not know frowning but is always smiling as a 
reflection of his inner joy. The early Church Fathers often stressed the positive side of 
fasting, which is nothing but opening the way before the human soul to ascend to heaven by 
the working of grace, to see our Lord by faith and rejoice in Him.  
Quite possibly, their attention was drawn to this principle by Christ’s advice to those 
who fast to anoint their heads and wash their faces (Matt. 6:17–18). There are perhaps two

St. Basil says, “Do not doll yourself up with gloom in an attempt to win renown by the 
appearance of self-control … Ostentatious deeds do not bear fruit that extends to the age to 
come but culminate in being praised by others.”432 
1024.  How can the believer offer his fast as a sacrifice of love? 
Through fasting, we declare the desire of our hearts to partake with our Christ in His 
sacrificial love. When the believer feels hungry or thirsty, he offers a sacrifice of 
thanksgiving to God who allowed him to partake in His cross or in His sacrificial love, and 
at the same time God inhales this sacrifice as a soothing aroma.  
St. John Cassian says, “The duty of fasting becomes acceptable before God when it is 
perfected with the fruits of love.”  
And St. Evagrius says, “When the soul desires to seek after a variety of foods then it is 
time to afflict it with bread and water that it may learn to be grateful for a mere morsel of 
bread.”433 
1025. How can we practice fasting so that we are led by love? 
The Church Fathers were saddened by those who fast by just replacing the types of food 
they eat, while still carrying within them  the desire for food and practicing gluttony . 
Through fasting, we save the cost of expensive food so we can give this money to our 
needy brothers an d sisters  — the least of Christ’s brethren  as He called them  [see Matt. 
25:40]. Through fasting, the believer’s heart and inner sight are opened to see the Lord of 
Glory in every person, especially in the needy and the suffering . For this reason, St. 
Augustine says that if one does not reserve some of his money during the fast to give to the 
poor, his fasting is without flavor . He also says, “Do you wish your prayer to fly toward 
God? … Make for it two wings: fasting and almsgiving.” 
1026.  How can we practice fasting as a sabbath to the Lord and find rest in Him? 
St. Basil believes that it is befitting for the believer to count fasting as a celebration of 
rest and the sabbath. The believer , his servants, and all the workers in his house, should 
mark the fast by not only finding spiritual rest, but also devoting the time normally given to  
cooking to spiritual worship  instead. He says , “The butcher puts down his knife and the 
table is content with plants. The Sabbath was given to the Jews, it says, that your donkey 
and your manservant might rest (Ex. 20:10). Let fasting be for your household servants a 
rest from their perpetual labors, seeing that they serve you for the whole year. Give your 
meat cook a rest. Give your tablesetter a holiday. Stay the hand of your winepourer. Give

odd matters here. The anointing of the head, especially in the first century A.  D., was not 
something practiced by men, youth, or children — so why is it necessary for them to do so 
if they fast? And the washing of the face is something we must do whether we  fast or not, 
so what need is there for this advice to those who fast? Clearly,  this is a symbolic invitation 
to live the life of joy. The anointing of the head refers to the ointment that is upon the head, 
the ointment of the Holy Spirit that comes down u pon Christ, our Head  [cf. Ps. 133:2] . 
Thus, the fragrance of Christ fills the world  through us, and the world encounters the fruit 
of the Spirit through our love and joy. And the washing of the face refers to the removal of 
dust from the face that we may s ee the Lord without any hindrance , and thus we witness to 
Him with the smile on our inner faces.  
St. Severus of Antioch  says, “ When Isaiah the Prophet raises them from this 
bottomless pit (i.e., their clinging to carnal matters), he raises them by drawing their minds 
upwards by declaring the greatness of fasting ; and so he impels them towards spiritual joy 
and expels grief and sorrow from their spirits, and implores them saying, ‘Is it a fast that I 
have chosen, a day for a man to afflict his soul? Is it to bow down his head like a bulrush, 
and to spread out sackcloth and ashes? ’ (Isa. 58:5). Therefore, when our Lord declares the 
splendor and joy of fasting, He also commands them clearly saying, ‘But you, when you 
fast, anoint your head and wash your face ’ (Matt. 6:17). He thus shows us that the 
flourishing and purity of the spirit are attained through the main members of the body. The 
Lord Himself commands us to wash ourselves and be purified by avoiding evil ; and on the 
other hand, to adorn ourselves by doing good deeds illuminated by spiritual grace.”450  
St. Augustine  says, “ We must understand this precept with respect to anointing the 
head and washing the face as referring to the inner man. Hence, to anoint the head refers to 
joy; to wash the face, on the other hand, refers to purity.”451  
1031. How is our Christ transfigured through the fasting of the Church?  
The purpose of the fasts of the Church is to entreat the Savior to work in all humanity.  
First. In w eekly fast s (Wednesday and Friday ): On Wednesday, the conspiracy to 
crucify Christ was hatched. Therefore, the believer fasts to thank God who turns the malice 
of the evil to the service of salvation. On Friday the believer sees, with St. Jacob of Sarug,

henceforth you will go forward on the royal way and your journey will be without fear.”423 
St. Cyril says, “‘He afterwards hungered,’ because, on the other hand, it was necessary 
that He Who refused not our poverty should withdraw from nothing whatsoever that 
belongs to man ’s condition, He consented for His flesh to require its natural supplies; and 
hence the words, ‘He hungered.’”424 
St. Isaac the Syrian says, “all strife against sin and its desires is to be preceded by the 
labour of fasting, especially if one is combating in ward sin.”425 He again says, “And also 
our Saviour, when He manifested Himself to the world at the Jordan, began from that point. 
For when He had been baptised, the spirit led Him into the wilderness, and then He fasted 
forty days and forty nights. And all those who follow His steps, base the beginning of their 
struggle upon this action. That weapon was polished by God, who should despise it without 
being blameworthy? If the lawgiver has fasted, to which guardian of the law is it not 
necessary to do likewise?”426  
St. John of Thebes  says, “Bodily fasting is abstinence from food, but spiritual fast ing 
is hunger and thirst for righteousness.” 
St. Jerome says, “After you have paid the most careful attention to your thoughts, you 
must then put on the armour of fasting and sing with David: ‘I chastened my soul with 
fasting,’ (Ps. 69:10) and ‘I have eaten ashes like bread, ’ (Ps. 102:9) … Eve was expelled 
from paradise because she had eaten of the forbidden fruit. Elijah on the other hand after 
forty days of fasting was carried in a fiery chariot into heaven  … and in Job it is written of 
behemoth that ‘his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly ’ (Job 
40:16).”427 
1022. Does God expect us to destroy the body when we fast? 
Fasting is the bowing down of the whole human  being before the Holy Spirit that He 
may sanctify him. God does not desire the destruction of  the body, but its sanctification.

records.question: Who was St. Demiana, and on which day is her martyrdom commemorated?
records.answer:
St. Demiana was a Christian martyr born to pious parents in the late 3rd century AD. Her father, Marcus, served as a governor in the region of El-Burullus, and she was baptized at a young age in a nearby monastery. Demiana is celebrated for her unwavering faith during a time of persecution against Christians. When she refused to renounce her faith and worship idols, she was subjected to severe tortures, including being pressed and slashed, yet she was miraculously healed by the Archangel Michael each time. Despite the brutal treatment, she remained steadfast, exclaiming her faith in Jesus Christ even as she faced execution. Ultimately, she was beheaded along with her companions, the forty virgins who stood by her side, and they all received the crown of martyrdom for their faithfulness [1][2].

St. Demiana's martyrdom is commemorated on the 13th of Toba in the Coptic calendar [2].

Soon after, the governor resumed his violence and cruelty towards the 
saints. He ordered the hanging of ‘Cosman’ and ‘Damien’ on two crosses, then 
to stone them. However, the thrown stones, before touching their bodies, 
reversed their course and headed towards those who were throwing them. As 
for their brothers, they were chained, cast betw een the two crosses, and were 
being shot with arrows from a distance, but here too, the arrows were returned 
towards those who shot them. That miracle caused all guards to flee. Then, the 
governor ordered them unchained and cast all of them into a fiery fu rnace for 
three days and three nights. God saved them from the fire. Then, the governor 
put them on hot iron beds; but the Lord brought them up unharmed. 
When the governor got tired of torturing them, he sent them to the emperor 
to deal with them. When the mother ‘Theodata’ strengthened her children and 
rebuked the emperor on his cruelty and his worshipping of the idols, he ordered 
cutting her head by the sword, and she received the crown of martyrdom. Her 
body remained cast on the ground, and nobody dared to bury it. St. ‘Damien’ 
cried out to those present: “O you inhabitants of this city; is none of you have 
mercy to cover and bury the body of this old woman? ” ‘Boctor,’ the son of 
‘Romanos,’ came forward, took the body, shrouded it, and buried it.  
When the emperor got to know what ‘Boctor’ has done, he ordered exiling 
him to Egypt, where he eventually received the crown of martyrdom. The next 
day, he ordered cutting the heads of ‘Cosman,’ ‘Damien,’ and their brothers, 
all of whom received the crowns of Life in the Kingdom of Heavens. 
When the era of persecution came to an end, several churches were built in 
their names, where the Lord performed so many signs and wonders. 
These saints are celebrated by the Church of the West on the 7 th of 
September and the 4 th Thursday of the Great Lent and by the Coptic Church 
on the 22nd of Hator and the 22nd of Paona every year.

DEMIANA AND THE FOURTY VIRGINS, SS. 
(The martyrs) 
Her Upbringing: 
St. ‘Demiana’ was born to two pious Christian parents near the end of the 
3rd century AD. Her father ‘Marcus’ was a governor on ‘El-Burullus,’ 
‘Zaåfaran,’ and the ‘Saysaban valley’ (northeast of Gharbiah governorate) in 
the Nile delta. When St. ‘Demiana’ reached the first year of age, she was 
baptized in ‘El-Mayma’ monastery, south of the city of ‘Zaåfaran;’ and her

idols gods when there is no god except the Lord of heaven and earth? I am 
prepared to die for His name’s sake, along with all those who are with me.” 
Provoked to anger, the leader ordered four soldiers to place the saint into 
the ‘Hinbazeen’1 chamber and to start her torture. The other virgins bitterly 
cried out when they saw their matron being pressed and her body being 
slashed. Then barely alive, the saint was thrown into prison. There, the 
Archangel ‘Michael’ came down at midnight and healed all her wounds. 
In the morning, the soldiers came to check up on her, expecting to declare 
her death to their leader, but to their amazement, they saw her free of any 
wounds. Provoked to anger, the leader assumed that ‘Demiana’ was a sorcerer, 
and he declared that all effort would be made to disable her sorcery. 
On seeing the saint was restored to full health, the multitudes cried out: “We 
believe in the God of ‘Demiana.’” So, the soldiers’ chief ordered killing them 
all, and considering that the saint was responsible for leading so many ‘astray,’ 
he put in his heart to double her tortures. He ordered combing her body with 
sharp iron combs, then rubbed into her wounds gypsum soaked with vinegar, 
but she kept being exultant, counting herself unworthy to partake of the  
passions of the Lord Jesus Christ. 
Then, she was cast again in jail. On the next day, the leader himself went to 
check on her expecting to see a corpse, but he almost collapsed when he saw 
her entirely healed by the Archangel ‘Michael’ who revisited her. He furiously 
tortured her in so many different ways: breaking her skull and skinning her 
body. A white dove came down from heaven, hovered above her, and healed 
her from all her wounds. 
Whenever that leader tortured her, the Lord was glorified in her. Finally, the 
leader ordered cutting her head off, together with all the heads of the other 
virgins with her, and all of them received the crowns of martyrdom.  
Before the sword struck the saint’s neck, the saint cried out: “I confess the 
Lord Jesus Christ; on His name I die, and by it, I shall forever live.”  
She was martyred on the 13 th of Toba. Her body is still there in the church 
built by Queen ‘Helena,’ the mother of Emperor ‘Constantine the Great’ (306-
337 AD), located close to the town of ‘Bilqas’ in the north of the Nile Delta. 
That church was consecrated by pope ‘Alexander I’ (312-328 AD) on the 12th 
of Bashons. Annexed to that church is the convent of St. ‘Demiana.’  
Several churches were built all over Egypt in the name of this great martyr. 
 [El-Mahaba Bookstore: The Biography of St. Demiana]

In the meantime, the King of Persia ‘Shapur II’ (309-379 AD) was on good 
terms with the Roman Empire and used to pay taxes to the Roman emperors. 
However, he changed his position and came with his army to fight the Romans 
in the days of Emperor Julian the Apostate (360-363 AD). Emperor ‘Julian’ 
offered sacrifices to his idol ‘Apollon’ in the city of ‘Casius,’ six miles from 
Antioch, then he marched with his army, accompanied by the diviners and the 
sorcerers, to encounter the Persians. 
Julian persecutes Domicius: 
When emperor ‘Julian’ was passing through an isolated site, he noticed a 
large crowd of men, women, and children; and he was told that they were sick 
Christians who came to get healing by the prayers of Fr. ‘Domicius’, the man 
of God, living in a cave over that area. 
The emperor was provoked to anger, and he sent a soldier to threaten the 
saint, saying: “If you dwell in this cave to please God, why do you seek the 
pleasure of dealing with people,  while you should have hidden from them? ” 
The saint answered him: “I have delivered my soul and my body into the hands 
of the God of heaven and earth; the Lord Jesus Christ, and I live as a hermit in 
this cave. However, those crowds who come to me with their strong faith, I 
cannot send them away.” 
On hearing his answer, the emperor gave his orders to shut the entrance of 
the cave with rocks while the saint was trapped inside. So, the saint eventually 
delivered his soul and received the crown of martyrdom in the year 362 AD. 
 [Baring-Gould’s Lives of the Saints: August 7] 
 [The Synaxarion: 27 Baramhat]  
 
DOMINICA, THE VIRGIN, ST. 
(The martyr) 
This saint was living at the time of emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD), and 
she was accused of breaking the idols down. The emperor ordered to cast her 
to the wild hungry beasts . However, the beasts did not harm her. So, they cut 
her head off around the year 303, and she received the crown of martyrdom. 
 [Butler: July 6]

the governor and the judge to the Christian Faith. He managed to succeed in 
convincing the governor but failed with the judge. Then, both ‘Lucius’ and

DELPHINUS, THE BISHOP , ST. 
This saint was the bishop of the city of ‘Bordeaux’ (in southwestern France), 
and he reposed in the year 403 AD. This saint’s fame was generated because 
of the letters he exchanged with St. ‘Ambrose’ ( 374-397 AD), and also, 
because of his influence on St. ‘Paulinus,’ whom he converted to Christianity 
and was baptized by him.

DEMETRIAS, THE NOBLE VIRGIN 
St. ‘Demetrias,’ this lady saint belonged to a noble family in Rome, and she 
dedicated her life to God i n virginity. Her grandmother, on her mother’s side, 
was so pious to be commended by St. ‘Jerome.’ She had three sons, all of whom 
were consuls. ‘Demetrias’ was longing for a life of virginity; however, she was 
afraid of the opposition of her parents, but they approved with joy and pleasure. 
The dedication of her life to God became the cause of happiness for all the 
churches. 
St. ‘Jerome’ (347-420 AD) encouraged her to study while she was pursuing 
a life of worship. He sought from her to be careful in choosi ng her friends or 
those among whom she lives. He preferred for her the life of fellowship rather 
than a life of seclusion; to practice the evangelic life among them; the way he 
previously guided ‘Eustochium,’ ‘Paula’s daughter;’ thirty years earlier. 
In the year 414 AD, St. ‘Jerome’ sent ‘Demetrias’ his letter # 130, in which 
he presented to her the basic principles to which she should be committed in 
her new life. His letter came to clarify the ascetic life in conjunction with the

DEODORA, ST. 
(The martyr) 
St. Deodora (Theodora/Didra) was the mother of the two martyrs ‘Abba 
Hur’ (Abahor) and ‘Bishai’ (Pishai). ‘Abba Hur,’ was a soldier in the army of 
Antioch, who came to Alexandria, where he confessed the Lord Christ before 
its governor. The governor ordered to cut his hands off, then to tie him to the 
tail of an ox to be dragged along the streets of the city, then he was cast into a 
pit full of serpents, which did him no harm. During all that torture, the saint 
kept asking for the help of the Lord Christ, who came to heal him and to 
support him. When his mother saw him in such a condition, she did rejoice for 
his strife. She then was reported to the governor, who called her in and asked 
her to sacrifice to the idols.  When she refused, he threatened her, and before 
her persistence, he ordered to put sharp, hot iron claws in her sides. During her 
torture, she kept singing and praising God who found her worthy to suffer for 
His Name ’s sake. She remained powerful until sh e delivered her soul and 
received the crown of martyrdom. 
Then, they put St. ‘Abba Hur’ in a pot filled with boiling oil and tar, in 
which he also kept praising God until he delivered his soul, and he too received 
the crown of martyrdom on the 29 th of Paona. His brother ‘Bishai’ too was 
martyred on the 1st of Nasi (the little month).

‘Besancon’ (in eastern France) and is commemorated by the church on the 27th 
of July.

DIONESA, THE DEACONESS 
On the 13 th of Baramouda, the Coptic Church celebrates the feast of 
‘Dionesa,’ the deaconess, who was appointed by the apostles. 
[The Synaxarion: 13 Baramouda] 
 
DIONYSIA, ST. 
(The martyr) 
In the days of persecution stirred up by Emperor ‘Decius’ (249-251 AD), in 
the year 250 AD, in the city of ‘Troas’ in Asia Minor; three Christians were 
presented to the governor, their oldest was a man called ‘Nicomachus,’ who at 
the beginning confessed his faith, and refused to sacrifice to the god, but when 
they started torturing him, and the pain was too much for him, he cried out, “It 
is a mistake. I never was a Christian; I shall sacrifice to the gods.” They brought 
him down from the tool of torture; but the moment he put the flesh of the 
sacrifice on his lips, he fell dead, as a denier. 
A 16 years old girl called ‘Dionysia,’ observing this scene, cried out. “Poor 
miserable man, for the sake of a few moments of pain, you earned for yourself 
indescribable eternal pains.” Then, she was brought before the governor who 
inquired from her if she was a Christian. She answered him: “Yes, I am; that is 
why I am sad for that miserable man who could not endure a few momen ts 
more to gain eternal comfort. ” The governor sought from her to do likewise, 
or else she would be tortured and burnt alive. 
The next day, ‘Andrew’ and ‘Paul,’ the companions of ‘Nicomachus,’ were 
brought before the judge, who decided to deliver them to the mob to stone them 
to death. Their feet were tied together and were dragged outside the city to be 
stoned there. Meanwhile, ‘Dionysia’ was led to receive her final verdict, when 
she met the crowd that was dragging ‘Andrew’ and ‘Paul’ to their death. On 
seeing them passing by, she managed to get away from her guard and cast 
herself on the two of them, crying: “Let me die with you upon the earth, that I 
may live with you forever in heaven,” but the governor denied her request and 
ordered cutting her head off by the sword. 
[Martyrdom in Christianity, p. 164] 
 [A. J. Mason: The Historic Martyrs of the Primitive Church, 1905, pp. 137 -9]

and come to me." 
Her Repose: 
Abba Daniel perceived that it was time for her departure, and he while wept 
bitterly. Then, he set forth to go to her with his  disciple, telling him: “Woe to 
the inner wilderness, for a pillar, will fall in it. Come, my son, bring the tools 
and let us hasten to reach the elderly saint before we are deprived of his 
prayers, for he is departing to the Lord." When they reached her, they found 
her severely ill with fever. After she received the Divine Sacrament, she made 
the sign of the Cross on herself, and her face shone, then she delivered her soul, 
and instantly, a sweet fragrance spread around the place. 
The two men wept, dug a g rave in front of the cave, and Abba Daniel 
instructed his disciple to shroud her over her clothing. Then, they buried her 
and prayed. On their way back, the disciple informed his mentor that he 
accidentally saw her dried up breasts. Then, Abba Daniel told him her story, 
and how the Roman elites diligently sought her and how no one knew anything 
about her up till that moment. 
She reposed in the year 576 AD. The Coptic Church celebrates her on the 
26th of Toba; whereas the Greek and the Latin Churches do on t he 10 th of 
March. 
 
ANASTASIA, SAINTS by that Name: 
(The martyr) 
The traditional books of Martyrs and the biographies of the Monks 
introduced to us many ladies who carried the name ‘Anastasia’ in the early 
centuries. The adoration of the Christians for the Lord Jesus Christ and being 
perpetually preoccupied with the power of His resurrection working within 
them made this name genuinely dear to them. Since the word ‘Anastasia’ 
means “Resurrection." In the following few articles, we shall mention some of 
the most famous of those who carried that name. 
 
ANASTASIA, ST.  
(The martyr) 
This Saint was martyred in the days of Emperor ‘Decius’ (249-251 AD) 
around the year 250 AD, and celebrated by the Coptic Church on the 1 st of 
Baba... 
She was the daughter of Christia n parents in Rome; they raised her in fear 
of God. Her heart was full of the Love of God, longing for the angelic life of 
virginity since her childhood. She joined a convent in Rome to practice the

337 
 
persist in disobeying the orders of the emperor. At the same time, he promised 
to add to their wealth if they obeyed. The saints, remembering the teachings of 
their parents and their good role model, they were not  terrified by the threats, 
nor seduced by the promises. They bravely answered him that they despise this 
world with everything in it , and were ready to die a thousand times than to 
deny the Lord Christ. On intensifying the mental and physical torture of those 
two virgin saints, Dimetria delivered her soul before her sister Vivian, and she 
received the crown of martyrdom on the 21st of June 363 AD. 
St. Vivian, who came to be lonely, by the grace of God, she kept unshaken 
before all those horrible events . Besides, she kept rebuking the cruel , unjust 
man on his evil behavior and sought from him to remember his end, and how 
it would be as dark as his heart. 
Vivian delivered into the hands of an evil Woman: 
To seduce Vivian to submit to his evil ways, Apronianus delivered her into 
the hands of a wicked woman named Rufina, who was extr aordinarily artful 
and was determined to bring her to another way of thinking. That agent of hell 
employed all the allurements she could invent , which were afterward 
succeeded by blow s. However, Vivian, making prayer her shield, remained 
invincible. On seeing that all his attempts ended up in failure, Apronianus felt 
that he ha d been severely belittled before that girl . So, he was provoked to 
anger and ordered that she would be bared naked, tied to a pillar and scourged 
with a whip loaded with lead plummets . Under that whipping, she delivered 
her pure soul into the hands of her true Groom , the Lord Christ, and she 
received the crown of martyrdom on the 2nd of December 363 AD.  
They left her body in a location without burial for several days to be 
devoured by the stray dogs and wild beasts. However, the Lord kept her body-
safe, and no beast could touch it . Eventually, a sa intly priest called John, 
managed to take her body and bury it beside her sister Dimetria and her mother 
Dafrosa. After a while, a pious Roman lady called Olympia built a little church 
in their names in the palace of their father Flavian. She also moved their bodies, 
buried them underneath the altar, together with the pillar to which St. Vivian 
was tied . In the Western tradition, the martyr Vivian is considered as the 
intercessor for people deserting the habit of getting drunk and also for the 
people who have epilepsy and severe headaches. 
  [The Martyrs: Vivian, Christine, Julia, Juliette and Auginie; p. 10] 
  [Saint Bibiana: From Wikipedia the Free Encyclopedia] 
       [Butler: 2 December]

morning.’ When all the brethren stood to pray in the morning, they asked 
the saint, ‘Tell this brother to stand up to pray, O father.’ The saint did, and 
the evil spirit came out of the man, and he was instantly healed.” 
Of His Words: 
A brother once asked the saint , “Father, what should  I do?” The saint 
answered him: “Keep quiet, and consider yourself as nobody.” 
“Have great care, you monk, to refrain from committing any sin, lest you 
insult God who dwells within you, and drive Him out of your soul!” 
   [W. Budge: The Paradise of the Holy Fathers, Vol.1, 2] 
 
BIBIANA (VIVIANA), THE VIRGIN, ST. 
(The martyr) 
A church was built in Rome under the name of St. ‘Bibiana’ (Viviana), in 
the 5th century AD. 
It was said that she was martyred in the days of Emperor ‘Julian the 
Apostate’ (360-363 AD). She was the daughter of ‘Flavian’ (Flavianus), who 
was the governor of Rome. He was known for his zeal about the Christian faith 
with his wife ‘Dafrosa,’ and on that account , he was fired from his position, 
was branded on his forehead w ith hot iron, and was exiled to a place called 
‘Aquapendente’ (the water of the bull), where he died in exile. 
The Western Church celebrates his memorial on December 22. As to his 
wife, she was put under house arrest, together with her two daughters ‘Bibiana’ 
and ‘Demetria.’ Finally, the head of St. ‘Dafrosa’ was cut off. Her memorial is 
celebrated by the Western Church on the 4th of January. 
The two girls ‘Bibiana’ and ‘Demetria’ stayed in their house, but they were 
in great need after all their possessions were taken away from them . They 
practiced prayers and fasting follo wing a harsh ascetic way for five months. 
However, the new governor ‘Abronianus’ kept threatening them every day of 
torture if they would not deny their Christ.  
Finally, he brought them for trial before the court of justice . During that 
trial, St. ‘Demetria’ fainted and collapsed, and then delivered her pure soul to 
the Lord. Then, the governor brought her sister ‘Bibiana’ to an evil corrupted 
woman by the name of ‘Rufina,’ to lure her to sin and to seduce her to deny 
her faith with empty devious promises . St. ‘Bibiana’ totally rejected all the 
advances of that evil ‘Rufina,’ and in spite of being beaten viciously by 
‘Rufina;’ sometimes using whips and other times by iron nails which tore off 
her flesh, the virgin ‘Bibiana’ endured the torture with great pe rseverance.

torment with great courage. The pagans kept screaming at them, seeking 
from them to save themselves by sacrificing to the gods, but the saints 
answered them, saying, “We are Christians, and we prefer to die thousand 
times than to do what you ask us to do.” 
After a while, the governor realized that he was defeated before them. So 
he gave his orders to his men to cut the Saints heads off. The saints, with 
courage and joy, approached the swordsmen while praying to God to have 
mercy on their souls, on those of all other men, and to save their fellow 
citizens from the darkness of idol worship. After cutting their heads, the other 
believers came and buried their bodies, which were moved to Rome. 
Later, the Fathers who assembled in the Council of Crete in the year 458 
AD, wrote to Emperor Leo I (457 -474 AD), saying. “The blessing and 
intercession of those Ten Martyrs have protected their country so far against 
the heresies.” The village where the saints were tortured was named “The Ten 
Martyrs.” Also, a large broken stone was discovered in the location where 
those ten saints knelt down to receive the crowns of martyrdom. They found 
that this stone had ten depressions resulting from the strikes of the shar p 
blade during the saint’s execution. 
 [Butler: December 23] 
 
MARTYRS OF DANDARA 
On the 16 th of Bashons, the Coptic Church celebrates the memory of the 
martyrdom of 400 martyrs in the town of Dandara (on the west bank of the 
Nile, about 5 kilometers south of the city of Qena). They were executed after 
suffering many tortures because they were Christians. This happened near the 
end of the reign of Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD). 
 [The Synaxarion: 16 Bashons] 
 
MARTYRS OF EDESSA 
In the days of Caesar Trajan ( 98-117 AD), there was a violent persecution 
against Christians in Edessa (El -Roĥa) in the Syrian section of Upper 
Mesopotamia. The bishop Barsimaeus (Barsamya) was arrested, violently 
tortured, and martyred in the year 114 AD. However, according to another  
version, he was only arrested but not killed; then, he was released after the 
persecution and later on reposed in peace.

records.question: How did he die?
records.answer:
St. Moses the Black died as a martyr. He was aware that a group of Barbarians was coming to attack the monastery where he lived. Despite knowing the danger, he chose to stay with his fellow monks, saying, "For a long time, I waited for this day, for the words of the Lord Jesus Christ to be fulfilled: 'All who take the sword will perish by the sword'" (Matthew 26:52) [3]. 

When the Barbarians entered the monastery, they killed him and the seven monks who had chosen to remain with him. It is said that after their martyrdom, seven crowns descended from heaven upon them, signifying their reward for their faith and sacrifice [3]. St. Moses completed his earthly life on the 24th of Paona in the year 408 AD, at the age of seventy-five or eighty-five, and he is remembered for his intense asceticism, love, and dedication to God [3][5].

Once four thieves tried to rob his cell, but he tied them together and 
carried them to the church. When the thieves r ealized that he was Moses, 
who used to be the head of a gang of thieves, they repented and wanted to 
become monks. St. Moses preached them with words that moved their hearts.  
Because of his great strife, the devils were stirred more against him, that 
his mentor Abba Isidore counseled him to moderate in his ascetic practices to 
keep them from causing him more troubles. He sought from him to deliver 
himself to God, and He alone would be able to alleviate that fight on him. 
Abba Isidore told him that, to keep  him from thinking that by his ascetic 
efforts, he could overcome the demons, but by humility and spiritual 
repentance, God would fight on our behalf.  
Ordained as a Priest: 
Because of his strife and virtues, they decided to ordain him as a priest. 
They arranged that the ordination would be performed at the patriarchate in 
Alexandria. However, the patriarch wanted to test Moses before ordaining 
him, so he ordered his priests that once they see him about to enter into the 
sanctuary, to drive him out saying: “Get out of here, O you with the 
blackface.” When they did that to him, the patriarch sent a deacon after him, 
and he heard him saying: “They did what you deserved Moses, for you are 
not a human, but dared to mix with men. Why then would you venture to sit  
among them?” St. Moses was ordained as a priest by the hand of the 23 rd 
Pope St. Theophilus (385 -412 AD), who heard at the time a voice saying: 
“Worthy, Worthy, Worthy,” and after putting the white robe on him, they said 
to him: “There you became all -white Moses.” He responded by saying with 
humility: “I wish this to be true on the inside as it is on the outside.” 
His Virtues: 
He lived denying himself that a governor, hearing about his virtues, 
longed to see him. When Moses knew about that, he ran away, bu t it 
happened that the saint passed by the governor in his way to the monastery, 
and he inquired from him about the location of father Moses' cell. St. Moses 
told him: “What do you want from such an old man, who is far from being 
upright.” The governor was disturbed and went to the monastery and told the 
monks about what happened. On understanding the monks how that monk 
looked like, they knew that it was no one but Fr. Moses, who denied himself.  
Because of his love, humility, strife, and intense asceticis m, he was 
granted by God to perform miracles and signs.  
A monk fell into a specific iniquity, and a meeting was held to discuss an 
appropriate penance. Moses was invited to attend, but he refrained from

passages.text:
240 
 
giving his sister Sarah in marriage and handing their whole wealth to her. 
However, when he discussed the idea with his sister, she responded to him by 
saying: “If you get married first, then I would follow suit.” He told her: “I 
have committed so many sins, which I intend to atone for by leading a 
monastic life, for I cannot get married and care for my salvation at the  same 
time.” She answered him: “How would you cast me in the snares of this 
world, and care only for your salvation?” Then, he answered her: “Whatever 
you choose will be yours.” She responded: “All that you would do, I shall 
also do, for we are of one fath er and one mother.” Then, they distributed all 
their wealth to the poor and the needy. St. Moises brought his sister Sarah 
into a house of virgins, and he joined a monastery near Alexandria, and for 
the following ten years, they did not see one another.  
Their Martyrdom: 
Then, when Emperor Decius (249-251 AD) incited persecution against the 
Christians, in the days of the 14 th Pope St. Dionysius the Great (246 -264 
AD), so many believers were martyred. At that time, St. Moises sent to his 
sister to bid her fa rewell, and let her know of his decision to be martyred in 
the Name of the Lord Jesus Christ. She hastened to her mother -superior, 
sought to be released, got the blessings of her sisters, and joined her brother 
on his way to Alexandria. There, they both co nfessed together the Lord Jesus 
Christ, and after being tortured by many tools, they had their heads cut off by 
the sword, and they received the crowns of martyrdom.  
 [The Synaxarion: 26 Mesra] 
 
MOISES, BISHOP OF OSIM, ST. 
St. Moises (Moses) was one of th e prominent fathers and saints of the 
church in the 8 th century AD. He was raised on the love of virginity and 
purity since his childhood, and he studied the church's various subjects.  
St. Moises became a monk, since his youth in the wilderness of the Sce tis, 
where he lived in the obedience of a great hermit for eighteen years, during 
which he walked along the road of virtue and harsh asceticism. He became 
known for his virtues that he was chosen to be the bishop of Osim (Ouseem), 
in the district of Embaba in the Beĥeira governorate. His life as a bishop was 
an extension of his monastic one in the wilderness. He was living in a life of 
deprivation and was known for his piety, courage, and zeal on the Orthodox 
faith. He used to spend most of his time in wors hip, that it was said that he 
did not see anyone, except on Saturdays and Sundays.

253 
 
going. When they insisted on having him, he came car rying a bag of sand 
with a hole in the back, which he explained by saying: “My sins run out 
behind me and I do not see them, but today I am coming to judge the errors 
of another. ” On hearing this, the assembled monks forgave their sinful 
brother.  
For some reason, it was proclaimed an obligation in the Scetis to fast for a 
week. During that week, some guests came to visit Fr. Moses. He prepared 
food for them to eat. On seeing smoke rising from his cell, the brethren said 
to one another: “Look, Moses has bro ken his fast and is preparing food for 
himself. We shall talk to him about it.” When they got to know the facts, they 
said to him: “Father Moses! You have disregarded the commandment of men, 
but kept that of God (i.e., giving hospitality to strangers).”  
His Martyrdom: 
Then, it happened that the Barbarians came to attack the monastery, an 
incident St. Moses knew by Spirit beforehand, and he sought from the 
brethren to escape. However, seven brethren stayed behind, and they asked 
him: “Are you not going to escape, father?” He answered: “For a long time, I 
waited for this day, for the words of the Lord Jesus Christ to be fulfilled: “ All 
who take the sword will perish by the sword” (Matt. 26:52). They said to 
him: “We shall stay with you and will not escape.” H e told them: “There, 
they are already at the gate.” The Barbarians entered the monastery and killed 
them all. However, when one of the seven escaped to the stronghold out of 
fear, he saw seven crowns coming down from heaven on the seven martyred 
monks. The n, he hastened to come down and ran forward to receive his 
crown of martyrdom.  
So, Abba Moses completed his strife on the 24 th of Paona in the year 408 
AD, when he was seventy -five years old (or eighty -five). He earned three 
crowns: the 1 st for love and i ntense asceticism, the 2 nd for monasticism and 
priesthood, and the 3rd for martyrdom. He was counted the first martyr in the 
Scetis, and he had so many great teachings. His body was kept along with 
that of his spiritual guide Abba Isidore in one tube at th e Paramus monastery 
in Natrun Valley.  
Of his Sayings: 
• To a brother in the Scetis who sought from him a word of encouragement, 
he said: “Go and sit in your cell, it will teach you everything.” 
• The man who flees from the world is like ripe grapes, but he who dwells 
among the distractions of men is like sour grapes.  
• If we keep the commandments of our fathers, I promise you that the

in the form of a girl. She managed to convince him to  spend the night at her 
place. Then, she claimed to him that she was the daughter of one of the kings 
and that she wanted him to marry her, quoting the honor of the marriage of 
the fathers: Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob. He accepted her request. Then, she 
claimed that she was a Jew, and he had to convert to her religion to be able to 
marry her. So, Moses was blinded, and he denied his Christ. Then, she (the 
deceptive devil) took him back to the wilderness, where a whole gang of 
devils ridiculed him and made so much fun of him. Finally, the hermit woke 
up and cast himself on the dust and kept crying and supplicating to the 
Compassionate God to forgive him. God sent him Abba Samuel, who told 
him that he would be departing after three days. Then, he took him to the  
church, where he gave him Communion in the Holy Sacraments after 
confessing all that the devil has done to him. St. Moses, the hermit, reposed 
in peace and was buried by Abba Samuel, who wrote his biography, and 
handed it to someone traveling to Alexandria for the benefit of the believers.  
 [The Hermit Fathers, Part 2, p. 25] 
 
MOSES, THE LIBYAN, ST. 
This saint was from Libya. He was so humble and compassionate all the 
time that God granted him the grace to perform the miracles of healing the 
sick. He once said: “When I was young, I lived in a monastery. There, it 
happened that eight monks dug a well, and seventy others built a wall around 
it, in the hope that they would get water from it. They dug it down to the 
depth of about twenty yards, but no water was found. They were very much 
grieved and intended to fill it up with dirt. However, by noontime, w hen 
Abba Pieour came over suddenly to the location of the well and was 
informed about what they were doing, he rebuked them saying: ‘Why did you 
despair, O you of little faith? ’ Then, he went down to the bottom of the well, 
and he prayed there. Afterward, he pushed an iron rod in the well bottom 
three times, saying: ‘O God of the saints, I pray, do not waste the effort of 
these men, but send them plenty of water.’ In a short while, the water erupted 
from the well and wetted everyone around.  
After praying a  thanksgiving prayer, Abba Pieour intended to go in his 
way. They tried to make him have a meal with them, but he said: ‘I have 
accomplished what I came here to do, I did not come here to eat.’”  
This was a good lesson for the brethren about faith and the trust in God.  
 [The Paradise of the Saints, p. 69]

master got rid of him. He turned into a gangster who lived on robbing and 
killing people. He had a large, muscular stature, which helped him to become 
the head of an evil gang.  
Having Faith in the Lord Jesus Christ: 
Even though an extreme evil -doer, yet he kept raising up his eyes towards 
the sun, believing that it was the true God, seeking fr om it to proclaim itself 
to him. Then, he heard a voice telling him to go to the wilderness to 
encounter the monks of the Scetis, whose fame was widely spread all over 
the area at that time. He went there, carrying his sword, where he happened 
to meet with  St. Isidore (The Priest of the Cells ) coming out of his cell and 
heading to the church. Terrified by his appearance, the saint asked him: 
“What do you want from here, O brother?” Moses answered: “ I heard that 
you are a good servant of God . Therefore, I es caped and came to you to let 
God save me the way he saved you.” He continued in persistence and with 
submission, saying: “I want to remain with you, despite my countless sins 
and my great evils.” 
St. Isidore kept asking him about his past life and where he  has been. 
Moses confessed to him all the sins he committed. On seeing how he opened 
his heart to him, St. Isidore started to teach him and preached him at length 
the word of God, he told him about the judgment to come and then left him to 
contemplate.  
For hating evil and deciding to rid himself of it, Moses shed so many 
tears, and deep remorse swept his soul and disturbed his sleep, like a dreadful 
ghost. Then, he went to St. Isidore, prostrated himself before him, and in a 
loud voice, he confessed all hi s evil crimes again, with such contrition of 
heart that drew his compassion. He took him to Abba Macarius the Great, 
who put him under his care, taught him and guided him, gave him the grace 
of baptism, then put him back under the supervision of St. Isidore.  
His Monastic Life: 
After a while, Moses sought from Abba Isidore to make him a monk. 
However, Abba Isidore started to explain to him how tough the monastic life 
is with the constant fight against the demons and the other physical needs. He 
told him as a way of testing him: “It is better for you son, to go and live in 
the populated areas,” but after seeing his real intention and solid stand, St. 
Isidore sent him back to Abba Macarius the Great, the father of the 
wilderness.  
Moses stood in the church and  confessed publicly about all his sins and 
evil deeds. Abba Macarius said afterward that he saw during Moses 
confession a whiteboard with black writings, and with every sin Moses

care for the sins of any man, good or bad. You should not do wrong to 
anyone, or think bad about anyone else in your heart or despise anyone for 
doing wrong. You should not obey anyone who harmed his neighbor or 
rejoice for him. You should never slander anyone, but always say that God

not have hatred against anyone. Do not have a grudge in your heart against 
anyone, and do not hate the man who is hostile toward his neighbor. This 
would bring you peace.

MOSES THE HERMIT 
St. Moses, the hermit, was born in Alexandria. Once he reached the age of 
thirteen years, he set forth to the wilderness of the Scetis. There, he dwelt for 
twenty years in a small cell next to one of the older monks. Then, he went 
deep in the wilderness an d lived for thirty -five years in a spot having olive 
and palm trees. There, he ate according to his needs whatever would fall from 
the trees, drank from the rainwater, dressed in palm leaves, and befriended 
the wild beasts.  
His Multiple Falls and Repentances:  
Satan envied this hermit, so he appeared to him in the form of an older 
man. The older man told him that he used to live a corrupt life, but he 
repented and distributed his wealth to the poor. He lived in one of the Five 
Western Cities (Pentapolis) near Cyrenaica (Barqa), and that God revealed to 
him that the hour of his death was approaching. They walked together in the 
wilderness until they reached a grand mansion. Then, the older man told the 
hermit that after his death, that mansion would be his, if he would marry his 
daughter. Moses was deceived and thought that the older man was on the 
brink of extinction, so he accepted his offer. However, once he declared his 
acceptance, he found himself amid the wilderness, hungry and afraid. He 
could not see any mansion there, and he realized that it was a trick from the 
devil. He felt how he was so weak and offered sincere repentance.  
Once St. Moses also went to Alexandria, where the devil appeared to him

Isidore who clothed him in the monastic attire. He advised him: “Remain, my 
son in this wilderness and never depart from it, because the day you would 
leave it, all evil will come bac k to you. Stay here all your life, and I am sure 
God will do mercy and grace on you and will crush the devil under your

His Strife: 
St. Moses started by dwelling among the monks. Yet, because of the 
multitudes of visitors, he sought from Abba Macari us to find for him a 
secluded place, and he guided him to a separate cell, where he dwelt 
tirelessly with such tremendous spiritual strife, in an attempt to make up for 
his previous sins and evil deeds. Even though the devil kept reminding him 
of his dark past, but his spiritual guide Abba Isidore counseled him to stand 
firm in opposing the old habits which were planted deep in his soul. He 
mainly complained against the evil carnal desires of Abba Isidore, who kept 
counseling him to stand fast until the dev il would get tired of him. He gave 
him an example of a stray dog that kept standing before the shop of a butcher, 
seeking to get something from him, but when the butcher did not respond to 
it, the dog had to go somewhere else. St. Moses was painfully attacked by the 
thoughts of adultery, so viciously that he could not stay in his cell. So, he 
went to ask help from St. Isidore, who told him to go back to his cell, but he 
refused, saying to the saint: “I cannot endure any more of it. ” Father. Abba 
Isidore too k him up to the roof and asked him: “Look towards the west.” 
There, he saw an uncountable crowd of demons, in great chaos, as though 
preparing for war. He then asked him: “Look towards the east.” There, he 
saw a great number of hosts of glorious saintly an gels, about whom the saint 
said to Moses: “Look, these have been sent by God to help the saints, against 
those in the west. Those who are on our side are far more than those who are 
against us.” Afterward, Moses was encouraged, gave thanks to God, and 
returned to his cell.  
Obeying the counsel of his father of confession, Moses fatigued his body 
by standing a long time in prayers, fasting, and doing metanoias. To 
discipline his body further, he used to go around the cells of the older monks 
at night, take t heir water pots and fill them with water from a well at a far 
distance from the monastery. Getting fed up with his harsh strife, the devils 
caught him once at the well, beat him so violently, and left him unable to 
move, until some brethren happened to com e to the well, and they carried 
him to the church to Abba Isidore. He cared for him for three days until he

258 
 
Emperor Valens sought to hold a treaty with queen Mavia and her people, the 
queen accepted on one condition, that the Emperor would see to it that the 
Egyptian monk Moses would go to Alexandria to be ordained as a bishop by 
the patriarch there. Although the queen was not yet converted to Christianity, 
she still made that condition to reflect the wish of her people. Emperor Valens 
accepted her situation because of his strong desire to make peace with those 
united tribes.  
Moses Refused to be Ordained by Arian Hands: 
On arriving at Alexandria, Moses found there Lucius the Arian archbishop 
who took over St. Mark's throne by force from the 20 th Pope St. Athanasius 
the Apostolic (328-373). All the other Orthodox bishops were in exile. Then , 
St. Moses stood amid St. Mark Cathedral and said with a loud voice: “Even 
though I am not worthy of the honor of a bishop, yet I consented in response 
to the love of those who chose me and gave me their trust. Yet, I shall never 
accept to be ordained by the hand of one of the deniers of the Divinity of my 
beloved Lord and Savior. If you let me be ordained by an Orthodox bishop, I 
shall accept from his hand this great honor. However, if you do not agree, 
then let me go back to my seclusion in the desert.” 
The Emperor's men tried in vain to make Moses change his mind, and they 
failed in trying to convince queen Mavia to stop her support for the monk 
Moses or to make her people choose somebody else. Finally, they had to take 
the monk to the nearest location o f the exiled Orthodox bishops, where he 
was ordained amid the exultation of the people. The people's joy was mixed 
with admiration of monk Moses, who bravely refused to submit to his tyrant 
opponents and exposed the falseness and helplessness of the Arians.  
Bishop Moses went to the flock that loved him and respected him, 
dedicated his life and effort to serve those who supported him against the 
opponents of Orthodoxy. He kept on moving from one place to another, not 
having a steady residence, teaching, preach ing, and converting multitudes to 
Christianity, and queen Mavia finally accepted the faith. He also managed to 
establish peace between his people and the Romans. Since then, the land of 
Arabia came under the St. Mark umbrella. Finally, St. Moses reposed in  the 
year 372 AD.  
 [The Story of the Coptic Church, Bk 1, p. 347] 
 [Baring-Gould: February 7]

records.question: What does St. Anthony say about practicing it?
records.answer:
St. Anthony emphasizes the importance of discernment in the practice of prayer, including the Jesus Prayer. He teaches that while one can engage in many acts of worship, without discernment, a person may deviate from the path of truth and holiness. This highlights the need for a mindful and intentional approach to prayer, ensuring that it is not merely a mechanical repetition but a genuine communication with God.

In the context of prayer, St. Anthony also encourages a life of continuous prayer, stating that one should bring oneself to account daily regarding what one has done in accordance with God's will and what has been done contrary to it. This self-reflection is crucial for spiritual growth and maintaining a sincere relationship with God. He advises that prayer should be approached with purity of heart and a commitment to living according to God's commandments, which aligns with the broader Christian understanding of prayer as a means of drawing closer to God and seeking His guidance in all aspects of life [2][4][6]. 

In summary, St. Anthony teaches that practicing prayer, including the Jesus Prayer, requires discernment, self-reflection, and a commitment to purity and holiness, ensuring that the act of praying is meaningful and transformative.

St. Anthony carried the garment of palm t ree fibers and presented it to

In the location where St . Paul the First Hermit used to live, a monastery

for the Lord. 
 
PAUL, THE MONK 
About Abba Ur (Hur), we know that he had a disciple by the name of Paul 
(Boulus) who cared much for the life of prayers, even though he 
misunderstood its meaning . He considered his prayers as a race to recite the 
greatest number of church praises. H e was eventually corrected by St . 
Macarius.  
About him it was said: 
He did not approach the hard handworks or the assignments of selling and 
buying; except for the littl e things he eats every day . However, he was very 
advanced in one thing, which was praying without ceasing. He set for himself 
a rule; to pray 300 prayers every day. He used to put some little pebbles in his 
pocket, and then he used to hold in his hand one of them for every prayer he 
prayed. One day, he came to St . Macarius, saying: “Father, I am very sad .” 
When the elder monk asked him the reason for his anguish, he answered: “I 
heard about a virgin who spent thirty years of her monastic life, reciting 500 
prayers every day . On hearing that, I despised myself, for I am not able to 
pray more than 300 prayers every day.” 
Here, St. Abba Macarius told him: “I lived for sixty years in the monastic 
life, reciting only fifty prayers every day; work ed for  what was e nough to 
earn my need of food; and receive d the brethren who come to seek my 
counsel. Now, here you are who pray 300 prayers every day, condemned by 
your thoughts. You probably, either do not pray them with purity; or you can 
do more of other things and you do not want to.” 
 [The Diocese of Beni-Suef: The Garden of Monks; pp. 24-25]

Book 6: Christian Concepts and Everyday Life 
333 
1191. To what extent can we grow in virtue with the spirit of discernment? 
True virtue bestows on us growth in attributes of a heavenly spiritual youth without 
progression to impotent old age. St. John Chrysostom  says that for the body, old age 
comes after youth. But the soul of a true believer will never become old, but will remain in 
a state of endless youth, if she so wills. He also says that the blessing (of baptism) is great, 
but if we will, it can become even greater. 754 The Christian do es not stop growing, as he 
moves from a state of spiritual childhood to spiritual maturity. And if he wills, he does not 
descend into weak and helpless old age but remains always in a state of renewed spiritual 
youth. 
St. John Chrysostom says, “While the one are punished justly, the others are crowned 
by grace. For though they had done ten thousand things, the munificence were of grace, that 
in return for services so small and cheap, such a heaven, and a kingdom, and so great 
honor, should be given them.”755 He also says, “For to flee from wickedness is not enough, 
but you must show forth also great virtue … the Judge henceforth is coming, His very self, 
the very Lord of the kingdom, leading unto greater self -restraint, calling us to heaven , and 
drawing us upward to those abodes.”756 
1192. What do the Church Fathers consider to be the most important virtues? 
St. Anthony the Great  asked his spiritual sons, the monks, about the most important 
virtues, and each monk spoke of his own preferred virtue. But St. Anthony he singled out 
the virtue of discernment, insight, or illumination, saying, “A person can practice many acts 
of worship, and without discernment he deviates from the path of truth and holiness.”757  
St. Clement of Alexandria  says, “Our transgressions being taken away by one 
Pœonian758 medicine, the baptism of the Word. We are washed from all our sins, and are no 
longer entangled in evil. This is the one grace of illumination, that our characters are not the 
same as before our washing [changing our ways]. And since knowledge sprin gs up with 
illumination, shedding its beams around the mind, the moment we hear, we who were 
untaught become disciples … For instruction leads to faith, and faith with baptism is 
trained by the Holy Spirit.”759 
St. Anthony the Great says:  
 
754 St. John Chrysostom, De Res. Dom. (on the resurrection of the Lord) (PG 50:441–442A). 
755 St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew 79.2 (NPNF I/10:457–458).  
756 St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew 11.3 (NPNF I/10:66).  
757 “St. Antony the Great” in Early Fathers from the Philokalia, trans. E. Kadloubovsky and G. E. H. Palmer 
(Faber & Faber, 1981): p.46. 
758 See Homer’s Iliad, v. 401. 
759 St. Clement of Alexandria, The Instructor (Paedagogus) 1.6 (ANF 2:216–217).

The Silence: 
Fr. Yousef asked the elder Fr . Nistherous: “What can I do to be able to 
control my tongue?”  Then, the elder asked him in turn: “When you talk, do 
you feel comfortable?” and the answer was in the negative. So, the elder said: 
“If you do not feel comfortable, why then do you have to talk? Would you 
rather not keep quiet.?  and if you were involved in a discussion , let your 
listening be much more than your talking.” 
I shall not Seek my Needs from Anyone: 
When one of the brothers saw Fr . Nistherous wearing two overcoats, he 
asked him: “If a poor man comes to you and ask s for one, which of them will 
you give him?” The Father answered: “The second one .” The brother asked: 
“If another comes to you asking?”  He said: “I shall cut the one I still have 
into two, give him half and cover myself with the remaining half .” The 
brother still asked him: “ If a third one comes seeking what is left on you, 
what will you then do?” T he elder said: “I shall give him all I have, and go 
somewhere to dwell, where God will cover my nakedness , but I shall never 
seek my need from anyone else.” 
The Work of the Monk: 
Fr. Nistherous said: “The monk should bring himself every morning and 
evening to give an account by saying: ‘What have I don e of what God 
wanted me to do? a nd what have I done of what He did not want me to do?’ 
This is what we should keep doing all our lives , and this was the way Abba 
Arsanius has lived since he cared to stand befo re God daily without sin. You 
should pray to God, the way you would in the presence of someone else since 
God is present with you.  Do not make yourself a legislator , and do not judge 
anyone. 
The monk who vows, perjures, lies, curses, slanders , or laughs lo udly; 
would be considered out of order and acting strangely haughty because, 
whoever honors himself and elevates it above what it is worth, will perish.”

Catechism of the Coptic Orthodox Church – Volume 2  
334 
“Some have afflicted their bodies by asceticism, but they lack discernment, and so they 
are far from God.”760 
“Helmsmen and charioteers gain proficiency through practice and diligence. Likewise 
those who seek the life of holiness must take care to study and practice what conforms to 
God’s will. For he who so wishes, and has grasped that it is possible, can with this faith 
attain incorruptibility.”761  
“Many have performed truly great labors of virtue, but have ruined themselves through 
folly. It would not be surprising  if the same thing were to happen to you too; if, for 
example, having cooled towards active work, you begin to imagine that you already possess 
virtues. For there you have already fallen into that devilish disease (thinking highly of 
yourself), thinking that you are close to God and are in the light, whereas in actual fact you 
are in darkness.” 
“I know that I am writing to you as to my dear children, and children of promise, and 
children of the kingdom. That is why I remember you night and day, that God may  keep 
you from all evil, and that you may continually have care how He may give you 
discernment and new vision, that you may learn to discern the difference between the good 
and the bad in all things. For it is written, ‘Solid food is for the perfect, who by reason of 
use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil’ (Heb. 5:14). These are they 
who have become children of the kingdom, and are reckoned in the measure of adoption, to 
whom God gives this new vision in all their works, so that none , neither man nor demon, 
may deceive them. For a believer can be snared by the pretext of the good, and many are 
thus deceived, since they have not yet received from God this new vision. That is why the 
blessed Paul, knowing that this is the great wealth o f the faithful, says thus, ‘I bow my 
knees day and night before our Lord Jesus Christ for them, that He may give unto them a 
revelation in order to know Him, having the eyes of their heart enlightened, so as to know 
what is the breadth and length and heigh t and depth, and to know the richness of the 
inheritance of the saints’ (cf. Eph. 3:14, 16, 18.) For since Paul loved them with his whole 
heart he wanted that great wealth of knowledge, which is the new vision be given to his 
sons whom he loved; since he knew that, if it were them, they would no longer have labour 
in any matter, nor would they be afraid with any fear, but the gladness of God would be 
with them night and day, and the work of God would in all things be for them ‘sweeter than 
honey and the hon ey-comb’ (Ps. 19:10). And God would be with them continually, and 
would give them revelations and great mysteries, which my tongue cannot utter.  
 
760 Benedicta Ward, The Sayings of the Desert Fathers: The Alphabetical Collection, trans., Benedicta Ward 
(Liturgical Press, 1984): p. 3.  
761 St. Anthony the Great, “On the Character of Men and the Virtuous Life: One Hundred and Seventy Texts,” 
in The Philokalia: The Complete Text, Volume I, trans., G. E. H. Palmer et al., eds., Nicodemus of the 
Holy Mountain, and Makarios of Corinth (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 1979): p. 332.

197 
 
The young man dwelt beside the River Nile and spent all his time praying 
in strict asceticism. Yet, when thoughts of boredom attacked him, he cried out 
to the Lord to guide him. An angel of the Lord appeared to him in the form of 
a man wearing a long robe, with leather cross-like Eskeem and a cover on his 
head. He sat weaving palm leaves for some time, got up to pray, then returned 
to work, and so on. The angel said to Anthony: “If you do so, you will never 
get bored." That  came to be the attire of the monks, and the work of hand 
happened to be one of the basics of the monastic life. 
One day, a woman and her maidservants came down to the river to wash 
their feet. Turning his head away, waiting for their departure, they start ed to 
undress to bathe. When the saint admonished her on such a behavior, she 
answered him: “If you are a monk, you should dwell in the inner wilderness, 
for this is not a place befitting for monks." On hearing these words, the saint 
said to himself, “This is the voice of the angel of the Lord rebuking me." He 
instantly forsook the location and set forth to the inner wilderness. That was 
around the year 285 AD. The saint dwelt in a cave on Mount ‘Al-Kalzam’ to 
practice the life of seclusion, North-West of the Red Sea. However, in that new 
location, the demons kept fighting against him, sometimes in the form of 
women and other times in the way of horrible wild beasts. 
His Order of Seclusion: 
In about the year 305 AD, he had to break his seclusion to meet with  some 
beginners who came to him longing to be trained under his supervision. He 
helped and guided them, then resumed his life of seclusion later on. Thus he 
was the founder of the movement of monasticism, his life revealed the concept 
of the Christian monasticism, particularly the order of seclusion: 
4- St. Anthony came out to be a monk without any intention to become a 
member of the clergy. His movement was a civic one, not a clerical one; he 
did not want to interfere with the ecclesiastical structure. Even, when 
Emperor Constantine I sent to him seeking his blessing, he delayed his 
response to the message, and when asked by his disciples why he did so, he 
said, “I am preoccupied to respond to the message of God, the King of 
kings." However, when he was pressu red, he answered the emperor’s 
message, for the sake of the Church peace. 
5- His intense love of seclusion did not close his heart toward the holy 
congregation, but, in his seclusion, he believed in being a member of the 
Church. That is why he eventually came  down to help Pope Athanasius 
the Apostolic (who was once one of his disciples). Moreover, on his 
entrance into Alexandria, the whole city was shaken, and its inhabitants 
came out exultant to welcome the man of God; that even some Arians 
came back to the Church.

Fourth: Purity of the heart. The scholar  Tertullian says, “Purity does not signify the 
washing with water, but repentance through the work of the Holy Spirit within us for the 
purity of our hearts and our entire inner and outer beings.”  
“But what reason is there in going to prayer with hands indeed washed, but the spirit 
foul?— inasmuch as to our hands themselves spiritual purities are necessary, that they may 
be lifted up pure from falsehood, from murder, from cruelty, from poisoning s, from 
idolatry, and all the other blemishes which, conceived by the spirit, are effected by the 
operation of the hands. These are the true purities.”267 
“After the whole  body has been washed and purified in baptism, there is need for 
purification through continuous repentance from the defilement of our hands.”268 
The scholar Origen says, “And it would be proper, when one lifts up his eyes and lifts 
them up properly to heaven, also to lift up holy hands, especially when he offers up prayer 
without anger and contention (cf. 1 Tim. 2:8). For in this way, when the eyes are lifted up 
through thought and contemplation, and the hands ae lifted up in deeds which lift up and 
exalt the soul, as Moses lifted up his hands (Ex. 17:11), one may consequently say, ‘The 
lifting up of my hands is as the evening sacrifice’ (Ps. 140:2); the Amalikites and all the 
unseen enemies will be worsted, and the Israelite reasonings in us will prevail.”269 
Fifth: Acquiring a mindset of truth . The scholar Origen says, “And so it was more th e 
soul of Anna that was cured of barrenness and bore fruit than her body when she conceived 
Samuel (cf. 1 Sam. 1:19f). Hezekiah begot divine children of the mind rather than such as 
are born of the body from the seed of the body (cf. 2 Kings 20:18; Isa. 39 :7). Esther and 
Mordecai and the people were delivered even more from spiritual attacks than from Haman 
and the conspirators (cf. Esther 6–7).”270

monastics?  
St. Basil wants the monk to attain to the vision of God and union with Him. Then the 
monk’s life — despite the intrusions of work and toil — is overshadowed by the Holy 
Spirit, hovering over him every minute and every hour. Then prayer becomes the air he 
breathes and the food that nourishes him. Theophan the Recluse says, “I remember that St.

Ecumenical Research Institute, 2005) 4.16: p. 92.

268 Cf. Tertullian, On Prayer 13 (ANF 3:685). 
269 Origen, Commentary on the Gospel of John (Books 13–32) 28.36–37 (FOTC 89:299).

passages.label: Catechism of the Coptic Orthodox Church, Volume 2, p. 37
passages.text:
Book 4: Church Worship as a Journey to Heaven  
27 
Fourth: Prayer expels foolish  ideas from our thoughts . The biography of Amma 
Syncletica of Alexandria, the disciple of St. Athanasius, says , “Therefore we must clean 
our house continuously and look around, lest any of the soul -destroying insects might 
penetrate into the treasuries of the soul; make hol y through sacrificial fire the places with 
the divine incense of prayer. For  just as one casts out the poisonous animals with the more 
piercing quality of medicine, just so prayer with fasting chases away foul thought.”62 
902. What practical steps lead us to practice prayer? 
First: Focus your inner gaze on God, your heavenly Father. St. Basil says, “When you 
begin prayer, forget every creature, seen and unseen, and begin to praise God, the Creator 
of everything; for it is said, ‘So He said to them, “When you pray, say, Our Father”’ (Luke 
11:2).”63  
St. Ambrose says, “Not everyone who prays ascends the mountain, for there is prayer 
that turns to sin (cf. Ps. 108:7). But whoever prays well, whoever lifts himself from the 
cares of earth to thoughts of Heaven, climbs to the topmost peak (cf. Ps. 23:3) and all his 
concern is things sublime. But there is no question of someone climbing to the top if he is 
loaded with anxious cares to get rich and to be a person of great importance. He is not 
going to reach the mountain -top if he is casting a covetous eye on some one else’s 
possessions. Only the person who seeks God will make the ascent; only the one who asks 
God to help him on his way. All great souls, all sublime and elevated souls, reach the top of 
the mountain. It is not simply to any and every one that the prophet says: ‘Get up upon a 
high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Sion. Lift up your voice with strength, you 
who bring good news to Jerusalem’ (Isa. 40:9). It is not with the footsteps of your body that 
you must climb this mountain, but by the sublimity of your deeds. Follow Christ in such a 
way that you yourself can be a mountain; for: ‘Mountains are all around it’ (Ps. 124:2).”64  
St. Evagrius says, “When the mind no longer contains images of earthly things  during 
prayer, it has become strong.” 
Second: Regulate the needs of your body in harmony with the hours of prayer. Let 
prayer take priority over the needs of the body.  St. Basil  says, “When you take food to 
nourish your body, you can scarcely be induced to leave the table before you have fully 
satisfied your need and, except for an urgent reason, you will not readily do so. How much 
more eagerly ought you to linger over spiritual nourish ment and strengthen your soul with

records.question: Why was he called 'Bishoy the Jeremian'?
records.answer:
St. Bishoy was called "Bishoy the Jeremian" because of his deep love for the Book of Jeremiah, which he memorized and cherished. It is said that when he read this book, he would see the prophet Jeremiah himself during his readings, which indicates a profound spiritual connection and reverence for the text. This special relationship with the Book of Jeremiah highlighted his dedication to the Scriptures and his ascetic life, as he sought to embody the teachings and spirit of the prophet [3][4]. 

His intense love for the word of God was a significant aspect of his monastic life, and he considered the memorization of Scripture as essential to his spiritual growth. This connection to Jeremiah not only reflects his personal devotion but also signifies the impact of the prophetic writings on his life and the lives of those around him [3].

His Love for the Salvation of All Souls: 
Saint ‘Bishoy’ had a disciple named ‘Isaac,’ who descended to the world 
and was seduced by a Jewish woman to forsake his faith, and he was converted 
to Judaism and lived with her . When he happened to encounter some monks, 
he asked them to tell St. ‘Bishoy’: “Your son, the Jewish ‘Isaac,’ has fallen and 
seeks from you to pray on his behalf to God to save him.” On hearing that, the 
woman said: “Even if ‘Bishoy’ come to me, I shall seduce him.” On returning 
to the monastery, the monks forgot what happened. Then, they were asked by 
the saint: “Has someone asked you to tell me something? ” They answered in 
the negative. The saint asked them whether they have encountered the Jewish 
‘Isaac,’ so they told him what happened and what ‘Isaac’ and the Jewish 
woman said. At that moment, they saw the saint retreat three steps backward 
and make the sign of the Cross on himself at each stage. Astonished, the monks 
said; “Even you, father, fear that woman?” St. ‘Bishoy’ humbly answered: “My 
children, the woman was the cause of the fall of ‘Adam,’ ‘Samson,’ ‘David’ 
and ‘Solomon.’ Who would be the poor ‘Bishoy’ to challenge her?!  Nobody 
can overcome the tricks of Satan in wo men, except that one whom God is 
with.” He kept praying and fasting for the sake of his son ‘Isaac’ until God 
saved him, and he came back and repented. 
Forsaking Scetis: 
In the year 407 AD, the first attack of the Berbers on the wilderness of 
‘Scetis’ took place. At that time, the monks escaped from the desert. St. ‘John 
the Short ’ asked St. ‘Bishoy’: “ Do you fear death, O man of God? ” He 
answered him: “No, but I fear a Berberian would kill me and goes to hell 
because of me!” 
St. ‘John the Short ’ went to mount ‘Kalzam,’ near the monastery of Abba 
‘Anthony’ where he reposed . Whereas, St. ‘Bishoy’ went to ‘Ansena’ (the 
village of ‘Sheikh Abbadah’ near ‘Mallawy’), and he lived in the mountain . 
There, he formed a close relationship with ‘St. Abba ‘Paul of Tamouh,’ and 
sought from the Lord not to be separated from him when they would repose , 
and God granted them their wish. 
St. ‘Bishoy’ remained in his expatriation until he reposed on the 8th of Abib 
in the year 417 AD, after reaching 97 years of age. He was buried in the castle 
of ‘Meniat el-Saqar’ near ‘Ansena.’ When St. ‘Paul of Tamouh’ reposed, St. 
‘Athanasius’ of ‘Ansena’ gathered the two saints'  bodies and buried them 
together in the monastery of abba ‘Bishoy’ in ‘Ansena’ (Monastery of El -
Bersha). The bodies of these two saints were returned to the wilderness of 
‘Scetis’ during the patriarchate of the 52nd pope Abba ‘Yusab I’ (831-849 AD).
